work.text: Kyosai painted a great many humorous and satirical works, so many indeed that to the majority of his admirers and critics he is known by paintings of this class alone.

source.author: Josiah Conder
source.title: Paintings and Studies by Kawanabé Kyōsai

work.text: Subjects which had long been used as art motives by painters in a [serious] and traditional manner, he would sometimes present in a new aspect by treating ludicrously, and into trite comical subjects he would often introduce fresh and [original] humour.

source.author: Josiah Conder
source.title: Paintings and Studies by Kawanabé Kyōsai

moment.text: During the political foment which produced and followed the revolution of 1867, Kyōsai attained a reputation as a caricaturist. His very long painting on makimono (a horizontal type of Japanese handscroll/scroll) "The battle of the farts" may be seen as a caricature of this foment.

matters.text: He was arrested three times and imprisoned by the authorities of the shogunate. … He again expressed his opinion of the new movement in a caricature, which had a great popular success, but also brought him into the hands of the police, this time of the opposite party.
